title: Fieldwork synthesis — small-model cascades and prompt orchestration
content:
Context and customer ask:
- Customer: mid-market adtech platform running real-time bidding (RTB) features (high QPS spikes, 3rd-party data privacy constraints).
- Ask: POC to evaluate a cost-latency-accuracy tradeoff for an on-prem/dedicated inference path for a classification + short-text generation workflow used in creative suggestions. Hard SLO: p95 latency < 120ms end-to-end (model portion < 70ms).
- Constraints: single-GPU target (A100 40GB) for initial private deployment, eventual Dedicated pool. Data is redacted creative snippets (avg 45 tokens).

Experiment goal: find a tiny-but-accurate cascade that meets latency SLO, with safe fallback and measurable economics. Emphasis on model-level changes (encoder pruning, structured quant) and prompt pipeline orchestration (retrieval/rewrite/generate).

Hardware & infra baseline:
- Target device: single A100-40GB (private pod).
- Serving runtime: Redwood Dedicated prototype stack w/ batching window tuned at 5–8ms, continuous batching enabled for burst smoothing. Triton-backed kernels favored for MHA paths.
- Baseline model candidates: Llama-2-7B, MPT-7B-Instruct, Falcon-7B (open-source equivalent). Also tried distilled sequence models (tiny-distil-1.2B) as first-stage filters.

Key experiments (summary):
1) Cascade design: tiny-filter -> quantized mid-size -> full-precision fallback
   - tiny-filter: 1.2B distill (float16), purpose: >65% of queries are trivial (rule-like), classify vs pass-through.
   - mid-size: MPT-7B awq-int8 + encoder pruning (remove 1 transformer layer + 10% heads) tuned for creative prompts.
   - fallback: Llama-2-7B float16 (no pruning) invoked on high-uncertainty bins.

2) Quantization matrix: AWQ-int8 vs GPTQ-int4 and dynamic 8-bit.
   - AWQ-int8 performed best stability-wise with tuned per-channel scales, minor loss in generation quality (~1.7% decrease BLEU-like metric vs float16).
   - GPTQ-int4 reduced memory footprint by ~40% but introduced hallucination modes on rewrite step; worse for creative output.

3) Encoder pruning (novel emphasis): we tried structured layer pruning targeted at early encoder layers (remove layer 1 and reduce attention heads by 10% in layers 3–6)
   - Rationale: early layers have diminishing returns on short input lengths and offer latency wins (fewer MHA kernel calls, smaller KV tables).
   - Result: ~12% reduction in per-token compute time (measured on trace kernels), 4–6% drop in generation coherence (human-rated), but still within customer acceptability for the mid-tier path.

Latency & cost numbers (representative):
- Baseline single MPT-7B float16: model p95 = 140ms (misses SLO).
- Cascade (1.2B filter -> MPT-7B AWQ+prune): model p95 = 52–64ms  (depends on batch concurrency), overall end-to-end p95 = 85–110ms with retrieval+postprocess.
- Fallback triggers: ~8–12% of requests hit Llama-2-7B fallback. When fallback invoked, p95 spikes to 220–350ms (acceptable if rare).
- Cost: estimated token-equivalent cost per 1k inference tokens reduced by ~38% vs baseline single-model float16 deployment (proxy using internal token-cost model).

Prompt orchestration (pipeline pattern we used):
- Step 0: shallow retrieval (local cache keyed by creative template) — constant-time lookup ~1ms.
- Step 1: tiny-filter classification (1.2B) — rules + classifier, returns one of {pass, trivial-suggest, escalate}.
- Step 2 (pass/escalate): run rewrite prompt on mid-size model (MPT-7B AWQ+prune). Rewrite prompt tries to normalize the creative snippet into structured fields (intent, target-audience, tone).
- Step 3: generation prompt uses structured fields and controlled sampling (top-p 0.85, temp 0.6) with guard rails.
- Postprocess: light deterministic cleanup + plagiarism/brand filter (on CPU)

Prompt examples (actual templates used in lab):
- Rewrite prompt (mid): "Normalize the following creative into fields: intent, call_to_action, tone_hint. If ambiguous write 'UNCLEAR'.
Input: {creative_snippet}
Output format: JSON with keys: intent, call_to_action, tone_hint."
- Generate prompt (mid): "Given intent={intent}, target={target_audience}, tone={tone_hint}, produce 3 succinct headline variants (<=12 tokens) suitable for display ads. Use active voice and include a CTA."

Evaluation methodology:
- Metric mix: human quality score (0–5), n-gram overlap vs reference (for rewrite), downstream conversion proxy (CTR lift simulated), latency P95, and fallback rate.
- Small A/B: 2k queries sampled from production traffic (sanitized) per config, human eval on 300 items.

Findings & tradeoffs:
- AWQ + structured pruning hits latency SLO with acceptable quality loss for 75–80% of traffic; fallback handles the rest.
- Int4 aggressive quant occasionally breaks structured generation (bad JSON), making downstream parsing fragile — not acceptable for rewrite stage. Int4 could still be used for pure scoring tasks.
- Pruning is most effective when applied conservatively to early layers; radical removal of middle layers produced lower latency but steep quality cliffs.
- KV-cache warmup: cold-start penalty of ~60–90ms for long histories; for short inputs caching helps only if repeated prefixes exist. Policy: enable prefix caching for user-session based flows, avoid cache for highly unique snippets.

Operational runbook (POC -> Prod recommendations):
1) Start Dedicated deployment with cascade: 1.2B filter (dedicated small pod) + MPT-7B AWQ+prune on single A100.
2) Canary: 5% traffic on cascade, measure fallback, human QA on fallback outputs for first 72 hours.
3) Fallback policy: soft time budget 180ms; if fallback triggers >15% in 24h, escalate to model tuning (reduce pruning or use float16 mid-model).
4) Monitoring: track p95 latency, fallback rate, parse-fail rate (JSON invalid), and manual quality-sample rate.
5) Rollout knob: allow dynamic prune-depth per route (config via Redwood Console) to tune quality/latency in real-time.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Should we move rewrite stage to float16 but keep generation stage AWQ-int8? Pros: better structured output; Cons: memory pressure. Need footprint assesment for A100 config.
- Explore hybrid quant: per-layer mixed-precision (float16 for attention, AWQ-int8 for dense) — schedule a micro-benchmark (Jira PRJ-8897).
- Long-tail failure analysis: characterize when fallback triggers and whether it's correlated to user segments.
- Customer risk appetite: acceptable fallback latency spikes and SLA burn thresholds.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: run per-layer mixed-precision microbench (baseline scripts in linked repo) — due 2025-10-10.
- Liam: implement dynamic prune-depth route config in staging console (feature flag) — due 2025-10-17.
- Noah: prepare customer-facing one-pager summarizing cost savings and rollback plan — due 2025-10-07.
- Maya: synthesize final POC report + recommend Dedicated compute sizing for scale to 5x QPS — due 2025-10-14.

Notes to self / workshop fragments:
- "Pruning felt like a hack but actually buys kernel-level wins because we reduce MHA invocations. But need to quantify memory vs latency trade in a reproducible benchmark."
- "Prompt orchestration reduces wasted decode; rewrite step is critical to keep generation small and predictable."
- Slack refs: #se-poc-adtech thread has some early logs (search for 'prune-win-0925').

Appendix (quick experiment logs):
- 2025-09-14: AWQ build v1 — per-channel scales tuned — quality delta vs float16: -1.7% (human).
- 2025-09-18: Prune experiment: drop layer 1 + 10% heads in layers 3–6 -> latency -12% tokens, human quality delta -0.4 mean score.
- 2025-09-22: GPTQ-int4 test -> hallucinations on rewrite -> revert for structured steps.

Bottom line (working recommendation):
Use a 3-stage cascade with a tiny filter, a mid-size AWQ-int8 model with conservative encoder pruning for the main path, and a full-precision fallback for high-uncertainty cases. Tie prune-depth and quant profile to a per-route runtime knob in Redwood Console to let customer dial quality vs cost live.

-- end of notes --
